pros: Captures global network structure, not just local connections
Recursive importance: influenced by important neighbors
Handles directed graphs naturally (in-links vs out-links)
Robust to manipulation compared to simple degree counts
Convergence guaranteed for connected graphs with damping factor
Scalable to billion-node graphs with distributed implementation
Provides interpretable probability distribution over nodes
cons: Computationally expensive on very large graphs (multiple iterations)
Damping factor is arbitrary and affects results significantly
Cannot distinguish between different types of connections
New nodes start with zero rank (cold start problem)
Memory-intensive for storing full transition matrices
Convergence can be slow for graphs with near-bipartite structure
Sensitive to link farms and spam (though more resistant than simpler methods)
Does not consider temporal dynamics of link creation
